item.title: Cyber Fire Puzzles (Fall 2025)
item.description:
💡

This event has concluded! See our Competition Winners at the bottom!

Join us this Fall semester at Auburn University for the exciting Cyber Fire Puzzles event, hosted in collaboration with Los Alamos National Laboratory! This two-day team competition focuses on solving challenging problems in logic, cybersecurity, computer science, and mathematics. Problems are organized by topic, helping you progressively build your skills and knowledge.

Who Can Join?

Anyone affiliated with a higher-level academic institution is welcome to participate! We encourage students and faculty/staff from Auburn and other universities to join us. All skill levels are welcome!

item.title: Weekly Meeting 3/4: PicoCTF Practicum
item.description:
Hello everyone!

This week will be a fun interactive session where you get hands on experience with CTFs. The meeting will introduce PicoCTF which has a collection of puzzles that range from beginner friendly to very challenging. If you are looking for a space to try out puzzles while receiving guidance, stop by!

The meeting will start with a short intro by Luke and Brad (me), then will lead into practical demos and practice sessions.

item.title: SECCDC Results!
item.description:
Hello everyone, over this past weekend EHC participated in the South Eastern Collegiate Cyber Defense Competition (SECCDC) and achieved great results with a final placing of 11th out of 38.

According to the CCDC website the mission of the competition is to:

“provide institutions with an information assurance or computer security curriculum a controlled, competitive environment to assess their student’s depth of understanding and operational competency in managing the challenges inherent in protecting a corporate network infrastructure and business information systems.”

item.title: CyberFire Puzzles 2024
item.description:
Hello everyone, we hope you had, or are having, a great summer. This year AUEHC will be opening up the fall semester with CyberFire Puzzles! This event is designed such that all skill-levels will find something engaging and will learn, so we highly encourage that you consider attending.

What is CyberFire Puzzles?

Created by the U.S. Department of Energy and Los Alamos National Laboratory , Cyber Fire Puzzles is a friendly competition that features a plethora of interesting mathematical and computer-science-based problems. You can expect to see sequence problems (think 1,5,9,d,…), number base conversion, network forensics, reverse engineering, and more. The problems in each category start at a beginner level but increase in difficulty as you learn from each problem.

item.title: ACM/EHC TechTalk
item.description:
This Wednesday the ACRC will be having guest speakers Michelle Leger and Will Zortman from Sandia National Labs give a lecture! Description is as follows:

ACM / EHC Tech Talk sponsored by the Auburn Cyber Research Center (ACRC) Sandia’s Digital Assurance for High Consequence Systems (DAHCS)
The digital foundations and security consequences of modern integrated systems

Short Abstract : This talk will explore a framework for thinking about open questions in the technical foundations for understanding digital system behavior in the face of threats, using evidence, abstractions, modeling, and system composition to make reasonable claims about a system’s digital assurance.

item.title: CyberForce Competition Complete!
item.description:
This past November 3rd and 4th we sent 6 AUEHC members to St. Charles, Illinois to participate in CyberForce, a DOE sponsored cyber-physical security event. The costs of the competition and travel were covered by the Auburn Cyber Research Center.

The goal of the event was to manage a fake energy company’s web portal and guard it from various threats. Students had to apply many cyber concepts taught here at Auburn in a high pressure situation.

item.title: AUEHC War Driving Results!
item.description:
On Tuesday October 17th we had our very first War Driving competition in which our teams recorded over 4000 unique WiFi networks throughout Auburn!

For this competition we used Kali Linux Virtual Machines, Kismet, and USB wireless adapters to track wireless networks we encountered. This was a great way to understand how many Wireless networks are in use in the world around us.

item.title: Tuesday Meeting 9/12: Game Hacking
item.description:
This Tuesday, we’ll be having a high-level overview of game hacking. This presentation aims to provide an overview of the various tools and approaches used in the realm of game hacking.

Planned Activities / Covered Topics:

1. Memory scanning: we explore the method of examining and altering game data in real-time.

2. Patching: a technique of directly modifying game files for permanent changes.

3. Trainers: specialized programs designed to modify game behaviors without directly altering game files.

item.title: Tracer FIRE 2023
item.description:
This past weekend (April 14-16), the Ethical Hacking Club and Sandia National Laboratory hosted a digital forensics and incident reponse (DFIR) competition called Tracer FIRE! Students from Auburn, Tuskegee, and Alabama State formed teams of 3-5 and collaborated with each other from Saturday morning through Sunday evening to find out what cyber attacks happened at a fictional company. More details about the competition below!

Students, faculty, and visiting guests at the Tracer FIRE 2023 event!

item.title: SNL Tracer FIRE Event Spring 2023
item.description:
What is Tracer FIRE

Sandia National Laboratories (https://www.sandia.gov) will be covering incident response, and having participants group up to work through a mock incident. This event mocks an actual compromised network and have participants investigate how the network was compromised, how adversaries moved around the network, and what was stolen from the network. Participants will work with disk images, memory dumps, and malicious binaries in order to understand and report on the incident.

item.title: SECCDC 2023
item.description:
In early February 2023, several members of EHC competed in the Southeastern Collegiate Cyber Defense Challenge Regionals round, a popular blue teaming competition where teams are tasked with protecting a collection of vulnerable machines from professional red teamers who volunteer their time to wreak havoc on university students’ attempts to beat them.

The competition lasted several hours and became increasingly chaotic, imitating what a multi-hour external attack on systems could look like. Mixed into the protection of systems, however, are customer requests from the fictional company that teams “work” for in the scenario.

item.title: Cyber Boot Camp 2022
item.description:
What is CBC?

Cyber Boot Camp (CBC) is an event hosted by Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) and Sandia National Laboratories (SNL). The goal of this event is to educate and train cybersecurity professionals and students in critical areas including incident response, and network archaeology. This year, the event will will be split into two hybrid events, one hosted by LANL and the other by SNL. Tentatively, SNL will take place January 6-7 and LANL will take place January 10-11.

item.title: DownUnderCTF 2021
item.description:
EVENT HAS CONCLUDED!

The public writeup is available below:

What is DownUnderCTF?

DUCTF is a worldwide CTF primarily targeted at Australian schools. Seven challenge categories with difficulties ranging from “sanity check” to “insane” were available last year, covering OSINT, forensics, web, crypto, misc, pwn, and reversing. We expect the categories to be similar this year.

When is it?

Start: 24th September 2021 at 4:00 AM CST (7:00 PM AEST)
End: 26th September 2021 at 4:00 AM CST (7:00 PM AEST)

item.title: CPTC 2021
item.description:
What is CPTC?

CPTC (Global Collegiate Penetration Testing Competition) is a competition that mimics real-world penetration testing conducted by companies. Unlike CTFs where you own machines and obtain flags for points, CPTC places greater importance on the written reports and presentation of results alongside finding vulnerabilities. Each CPTC has a different theme which has an impact on the types of systems under test. This year’s theme is a retail bakery, so expect e-commerce to play a heavy role. They’ll also likely have some industrial control systems stuff (as bakers do).

item.title: CyberFire Puzzles Fall 2021 Report
item.description:
The Fall 2021 Cyber Fire Puzzles are complete! We want to say thank you and congratulations to everyone that participated, and we hope you had fun and learned some new tricks and tools along the way! Below is a brief writeup that details the total number of participants, the teams and their placements, the challenge categories offered, and the overall event results.

Introduction

The Fall 2021 Cyber Fire Puzzles ran from 11 AM CDT on Saturday, August 21, to 5 PM CDT the next day, August 22, giving a little over 24 hours for all the participants to solve challenges. There were **37 total applicants, with a mix of PhD, Master’s, and undergradute students all participating. The event was offered both online and in person, with some teams competing in person, some teams competing online, and some teams having both in person and online participants, using the AUEHC Discord to communicate.

item.title: CyberFire Puzzles Fall 2021 Details
item.description:
What is CyberFire Puzzles?

CyberFire Puzzles are beginner-friendly cyber security challenges created by the U.S. Department of Energy and Los Alamos National Laboratory The challenges cover a variety of cyber security topics and offer participants the opportunity to learn more about the field.

Can I work with a team?

Participants can work in teams or alone. If you don’t have a team, we can help you find one. Cyber Fire Puzzles offers a great opportunity to gain experience working on cyber security problems and looks good on your resume and to employers.

item.title: Cyber Boot Camp 2021 Details
item.description:
What is Cyber Boot Camp 2021?

Cyber Boot Camp 2021 (CBC ‘21) is two separate events that are being hosted by Los Alamos National Laboratory and Sandia National Laboratories. Collectively, the goal of CBC ‘21 is to educate and train cyber-security professionals and students in critical areas including digital forensics incident response, forensic investigations, and analysis. CBC ‘21 is broken up into two separate events that will take place in early January.
